subject: Prod: SparrowData latency spike — KV restore/throughput
messages:
From: Sasha Li <sasha.li@sparrowdata.com>

Cc: ops@sparrowdata.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike: Redwood inference impacting queries

Jordan / Redwood team,

We're seeing a severe latency spike and an increase in 5xx errors across our live inference traffic starting ~14:30 PDT. Tail p99 latency jumped from ~210ms to 2.4s and throughput fell by ~40%. We tried routing a subset to a smaller model to reduce tokens but errors persisted. This is impacting Sparrows's customer-facing search results and several large customers are complaining in parallel.

Attached are a short sampling of logs and the stack traces (sparrow-logs-20280721.zip). Key observations from our side:
- Error rate (5xx) climbed from 0.3% -> 3.8% over 30 minutes
- Throughput drop correlates with bursts of cache rehydration activity per-tenant
- We see repeated retries and long queue lengths in traces that look like head-of-line blocking.

We need an immediate triage call and a remediation plan. If you can indicate an ETA and whether you can route us to a fallback path or dedicated pool, that would help calm affected customers.

—Sasha
Sasha Li
Head of Platform Reliability, SparrowData

TL;DR: Observed concurrent KV restore races causing HOL blocking and cache thrash for sparrow-main-01 tenants; proposed emergency knobs and timeline below.

What I found (quick triage):
- At ~14:22 PDT we see a wave of tenant rehydrate requests after a failed autoscaler event. Multiple restore threads attempt to re-populate the same key ranges concurrently.
- Restore duration distribution shows a heavy tail (mean 110ms, 95th 2.1s) and we see per-tenant queue growth that blocks subsequent request batches (hot-lane HOL).
- Batching layer is accumulating large batches because many requests are stalled behind the same key range; this reduces token throughput and makes the scheduler backpressure propagate system-wide.
- Kernel-level metrics show repeated small allocations and GC churn during these restore bursts (see kernel-stats.txt attached).

Immediate mitigations I can apply (30–45 mins):
1) Drop kv_restore_concurrency for the affected pool from 16 -> 4 to serialize restore work and avoid thrash (will increase individual restore latency but prevents HOL blocking).
2) Enable per-tenant cache pinning for sparrow-main-01 so restores do not evict each other while the pool warms.
3) Route 20% of traffic for the largest tenant shards to a cold-safe fallback model (lower capacity but avoids access to the contested cache path).

Longer-term (post-mitigation):
- Add restore-coalescing at the KV layer (coalesce identical key-range restores), improve pre-warming heuristics, and add a priority lane for small latencies.

I'll prepare a short exec-friendly summary if we need leadership signoff for capacity or customer credits. If you want me to apply the emergency knobs now, say go and I'll push a targeted change to the dedicated pool.

—Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Leaders — quick summary and ask:

What happened: Concurrent KV restore activity during an autoscaler flap caused head-of-line blocking in the batching layer for SparrowData's primary tenant. The result was elevated p99 latency (~2.4s), higher 5xx rates (up to 3.8%), and a ~40% throughput reduction between 14:20–15:30 PDT.

Impact: Major customer (SparrowData) experiencing visible customer-facing errors; they've escalated to their executive team. Potential churn risk if we don't resolve within the next window.

Immediate mitigation proposed (Jonas recommends):
- Reduce kv_restore_concurrency on affected pool (emergency config)
- Temporarily pin cache entries for sparrow-main-01
- Route a small % of heavy shards to fallback model while pool stabilizes

Asks for execs:
1) Approve allocation of an ad-hoc dedicated GPU pool for SparrowData for the next 72 hours if the configuration knobs do not bring p99 under 500ms. This is billable but we'll consider credits if SLA impact is confirmed.
2) Approve a customer comms template offering a 10% platform credit if service-levels are not restored within 24 hours.

I'll hold on applying the routing-to-dedicated change until I have approval; Jonas can push config knobs immediately. Suggest we brief the customer at 17:00 PDT (in 20–30 mins).

—Jordan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
